concepts.name: Evolution of CRZ Notifications: 1991 → 2011 → 2019
key_dimensions: Key shifts in classification criteria and permissible activities across three generations of notifications
Why each revision was necessitated — developmental pressure vs. ecological concerns
Introduction of new zones (CRZ-IVA, IVB in 2019) absent in earlier versions
UPSC trap: conflating provisions of 2011 with 2019 — what was added, removed, or relaxed

concepts.name: Coastal Regulation Zone vs. High Tide Line (HTL): Definitional Precision
key_dimensions: Technical definition of HTL under CRZ notifications and how it is measured
How the CRZ boundary is drawn with reference to HTL (landward vs. seaward extent)
Distinction between HTL and Low Tide Line (LTL) and their regulatory relevance
UPSC trap: assuming CRZ applies only landward — the seaward extent covering territorial waters up to 12 nautical miles

concepts.name: CRZ Classification: CRZ-I, II, III, IV — Criteria and Permissible Activities
key_dimensions: Ecological basis for CRZ-I (ecologically sensitive areas) vs. developmental basis for CRZ-II (built-up municipal areas)
CRZ-III distinction between rural and urban areas under 2019 notification and revised NDZ widths
CRZ-IV covering water area from LTL to 12 nautical miles — often overlooked in preparation
UPSC trap: which activities are permitted vs. prohibited within each sub-zone — especially construction near HTL

concepts.name: No Development Zone (NDZ): Width Variations and Exceptions
key_dimensions: Standard NDZ widths under 2019: 50m for CRZ-III urban, 200m for CRZ-III rural, 20m for backwaters/creeks
How NDZ width changed from 2011 to 2019 — reduction controversy and its rationale
Activities exempted from NDZ restrictions (fishing communities, defence, heritage structures)
UPSC trap: NDZ is not uniform — varies by zone type, proximity to population centres, and water body type

concepts.name: CRZ-IA vs. CRZ-IB: Sub-classification of Ecologically Sensitive Areas
key_dimensions: CRZ-IA includes mangroves, coral reefs, salt marshes, turtle nesting grounds, horseshoe crab habitats
CRZ-IB includes land between HTL and LTL (intertidal zone) — significance for construction prohibition
Absolute prohibition on construction in CRZ-IA vs. conditional restrictions in other zones
UPSC trap: mangroves covered under CRZ-IA but also separately under Forest Conservation Act — dual protection framework

concepts.name: Coastal Zone Management Plans (CZMPs): Preparation, Approval, and Legal Status
key_dimensions: Role of State/UT governments and Coastal Zone Management Authorities in preparing CZMPs
MoEFCC's approval process and the binding nature of approved CZMPs
Relationship between CZMPs and District-level spatial planning — hierarchy of plans
UPSC trap: CZMPs are mandatory under CRZ but many states have pending/rejected plans — implications for development permissions

concepts.name: Coastal Zone Management Authorities (CZMAs): Structure and Jurisdiction
key_dimensions: National CZMA vs. State/UT CZMAs — respective powers and composition
CZMAs as statutory bodies under Environment Protection Act 1986 — not independent legislation
Enforcement powers of CZMAs including power to recommend cancellation of projects
UPSC trap: CZMAs are monitoring/regulatory bodies, not the approving authority for all CRZ projects — distinction between project-level clearance and policy oversight

concepts.name: Special Provisions for Island Territories: Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep
key_dimensions: Separate Island Protection Zone (IPZ) notification replacing CRZ for island territories
NDZ of 50m from HTL for islands vs. different widths for mainland — rationale
2019 notification allowing beach resorts in CRZ areas of islands to promote eco-tourism — controversy
UPSC trap: Islands are NOT governed by CRZ 2019 in the same manner — IPZ is a distinct notification

concepts.name: Fishing Communities and Traditional Rights Under CRZ
key_dimensions: Special provisions allowing dwelling units and fish drying yards for traditional fishing communities within NDZ
Bona fide local community facilities (schools, dispensaries) permitted in CRZ — conditions
Conflict between CRZ protections and displacement of fishing communities for port/tourism projects
UPSC trap: fishing community rights are NOT absolute — restricted to traditional/local fisherfolk, not commercial fishing enterprises

concepts.name: Permissible vs. Prohibited Activities in CRZ: Categories and Nuances
key_dimensions: Activities requiring CRZ clearance (conditional permissions) vs. those absolutely prohibited
Mining of sand, rocks, coral extraction — prohibited across all CRZ zones
Thermal power plants, ports, and tourism infrastructure — zone-specific permissibility
UPSC trap: desalination plants and renewable energy projects have zone-specific conditional permissions — not uniformly allowed or banned

concepts.name: CRZ 2019: Key Liberalisations and Their Controversies
key_dimensions: Reduction of NDZ for urban CRZ-III from 200m to 50m — rationale of aligning with CRZ-II
Floor Space Index (FSI) relaxation for reconstruction of old buildings in CRZ — implications for Mumbai
Permitting temporary tourism facilities like beach shacks on a seasonal basis
UPSC trap: the 2019 notification is often characterised as 'development-friendly' — but it also added stricter protections for mangroves and coral reefs; balanced critique required

concepts.name: Setback Lines: Hazard Line vs. HTL-based NDZ
key_dimensions: Hazard Line demarcated by Survey of India incorporating impacts of sea-level rise, tidal flooding, and erosion — distinct from HTL
Hazard Line used for disaster management planning, not for CRZ regulatory boundary determination
Overlap and conflict between Hazard Line and CRZ NDZ in low-lying coastal states
UPSC trap: Hazard Line is NOT the basis for CRZ — it is used for state-level disaster planning and insurance purposes only

concepts.name: CRZ Clearance Process: Hierarchy and Delegated Powers
key_dimensions: Projects with investment above threshold require MoEFCC clearance; below threshold delegated to State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA)
Role of Ministry of Environment vs. State CZMAs in granting clearances — no duplication
Public consultation requirements under EIA Notification 2006 as applicable to CRZ projects
UPSC trap: CRZ clearance and EIA clearance are separate processes — some projects need both, creating confusion about which authority is primary

concepts.name: Mangrove Conservation Under CRZ: Special Protections and Buffer Zones
key_dimensions: 50m buffer zone mandatory around mangrove areas of any size under 2019 notification — improvement over 2011
Mangroves notified as CRZ-IA regardless of their area — even small patches qualify
Intersection of CRZ mangrove protection with Forest Rights Act and State Forest Acts
UPSC trap: mangroves on private land also attract CRZ-IA protection — ownership does not override ecological classification

concepts.name: Judicial Interventions in CRZ Implementation: Key Supreme Court and NGT Rulings
key_dimensions: Supreme Court in Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India on coastal protection and state obligations
NGT orders on demolition of illegal constructions within NDZ and state government inaction
Court directions on finalisation of pending CZMPs and CZMA constitution
UPSC trap: courts have both upheld and struck down CRZ relaxations — judicial trend is not uniformly restrictive; depends on site-specific ecological sensitivity

concepts.name: Coastal Aquaculture and CRZ: Conditional Permissions and Conflicts
key_dimensions: Coastal Aquaculture Authority Act 2005 as a separate regulatory framework — interplay with CRZ
Shrimp farming and its historical conflict with CRZ (Supreme Court 1996 order banning shrimp farming in CRZ)
Permitted vs. prohibited forms of aquaculture in different CRZ categories under 2019 notification
UPSC trap: aquaculture is not uniformly banned — traditional and modified extensive aquaculture is permitted in certain CRZ zones with conditions

concepts.name: Port, Harbour, and Waterfront Development Under CRZ
key_dimensions: Ports and harbour construction requiring special CRZ clearances and mandatory EIA
Distinction between major ports (Union List, central jurisdiction) and minor ports (State List) in CRZ clearance procedures
Coastal Economic Zones and Sagarmala project infrastructure versus CRZ restrictions — policy tension
UPSC trap: maritime infrastructure projects often invoke 'national interest' exemptions — but no blanket exemption exists; case-by-case clearance is mandatory

concepts.name: Tidal Wetlands, Salt Pans, and Mudflats: Classification and Protection Gaps
key_dimensions: Salt pans classified as CRZ-I — absolute protection; cannot be converted to residential/commercial use
Mumbai's salt pan land conversion controversy as a recurring UPSC-relevant case study
Mudflats and tidal wetlands as critical bird habitats overlapping with Ramsar site designations
UPSC trap: CRZ classification of salt pans protects them from development but does not prevent them from being leased for salt extraction — functional vs. structural protection

concepts.name: Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) Project and Its Relationship with CRZ
key_dimensions: ICZM as a World Bank-assisted initiative implemented in Odisha, Gujarat, and West Bengal pilot states
ICZM goes beyond CRZ regulation — includes livelihood support, shoreline management, and capacity building
National ICZM Policy (draft) and its vision for moving from 'regulation-only' to 'integrated management' approach
UPSC trap: ICZM is a project/policy initiative, NOT a replacement for CRZ notifications — they operate in parallel with different mandates

concepts.name: Shoreline Change and Sea-Level Rise: CRZ Adaptation Challenges
key_dimensions: CRZ notifications based on static HTL — vulnerability to dynamic shoreline changes due to erosion, accretion, and sea-level rise
IPCC projections on sea-level rise for Indian coastline and inadequacy of current NDZ widths
Correlation between CRZ violations and increased vulnerability during cyclones and storm surges (lessons from Fani, Amphan, Biparjoy)
UPSC trap: CRZ is a regulatory tool, not a climate adaptation strategy — the gap between static CRZ boundaries and dynamic coastal processes is a critical policy weakness
